title: Novena for Finding Love
kicker: 9 days of hope for finding love
card: For anyone hoping for someone to share life with: 9 days asking for a ready heart, wise discernment and trust in God’s timing.
ogDescription: 9 days of prayer for finding love, through Our Lady, St. Raphael and Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin.
description: A 9-day Catholic novena for finding love and a partner for life, through Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, St. Raphael and Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin.

epigraph.text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it.

closingVerse.text: For I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope.

saints.name: St. Raphael
saints.bio: Archangel of the Book of Tobit, who stands before God and brings Him the prayers of His people. Unrecognized, he guided young Tobias on a long journey, during which Tobias met and married Sarah.
saints.alt: Painting: the Archangel Raphael, by Giovanni Biliverti
saints.openingRole: faithful guide of Tobias and Sarah

saints.name: St. Louis Martin
saints.bio: Watchmaker of Alençon, France. He hoped to join the canons of the Great St. Bernard Hospice, but was turned away. He married Zélie Guérin in 1858 and was the father of St. Thérèse.
saints.openingRole: who sought God’s will and found it in marriage

saints.name: St. Zélie Martin
saints.bio: Lacemaker of Alençon who ran her own lace business. Turned away by the Daughters of Charity, she married Louis Martin in 1858. Mother of nine, including St. Thérèse; she died of cancer at 45.
saints.openingRole: who loved her family with a brave heart

openingPrayer: Heavenly Father, You made us for love, and You know the longing of N. for someone to share life with. We bring this hope to You honestly, with its joy, its loneliness and its waiting. Make N. ready to give and receive love, give them wisdom to recognize a good and faithful heart, and teach them to trust Your timing more than their own. Today we ask Mary, Mother of Fairest Love; St. Raphael, faithful guide of Tobias and Sarah; and Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin, who found each other in God’s time, to join their prayers with ours, through Christ our Lord.
closingPrayer: Lord Jesus, who brought joy to the wedding at Cana, walk with N. on the path of love. Prepare their heart, guide their steps and choices, and let Your holy will be done.

tips.p: One person leads each part; all respond pray for us and Amen, and say the closing prayers together. The prayers say “we”; if you pray alone, say “I”.

If you can, go to Confession and attend Mass during these 9 days. Pair prayer with action: say yes to good invitations, meet people through your parish, friends and community, and ask someone you trust for honest advice (Day 5). With people you meet online, meet in a public place and never send money. A medal or statue is a sign of prayer, not a charm. At “N.”, say the person’s name, or “me” if you pray for yourself; if you pray for someone else, offer each day’s step for them.

tips.h: If love is slow to come
tips.p: Waiting is not a sign that something is wrong with you, or that you prayed too little. Your worth does not depend on being chosen (Day 2). If you are healing from a breakup or a love that was not returned, take your time: God is patient with every heart. If a past relationship hurt you or left you feeling unsafe, talk to someone you trust and get the help you need. If you were married before, speak with a priest about your situation before beginning a new relationship.

intentionPlaceholder: Write who you are praying for, and the graces you ask: a ready heart, wisdom, patience.

days.title: Bringing Our Longing to God
days.verse: The prayer of both was heard in the presence of the glory of the great God.
days.refl: On the same day, in two different cities, two people poured out their hearts to God: old Tobit, blind and discouraged, and young Sarah, who had known deep sorrow in marriage. Neither could see how their stories would meet. Yet Scripture says both prayers were heard. The longing to love and be loved is nothing to hide or be ashamed of. God placed it in us. So we begin these nine days by telling Him honestly what we hope for, and trusting that He hears.
days.more: Sarah’s grief was real. She had been given in marriage seven times, and each husband had died on the wedding night; even her father’s maids taunted her. In her distress she turned to God and prayed by her window (Tobit 3). At that very hour, God sent Raphael to help both her and Tobit. Whatever lies behind us, we can bring it to the God who hears.
days.prayer: Heavenly Father, You heard the prayers of Tobit and Sarah on the same day, and You hear us now. We bring You the longing of N. for someone to share life with: their hopes, their loneliness, and any hurt from the past. Through the prayers of St. Raphael, help N. to speak to You honestly, and to trust that You know their heart even better than they do.
days.step: Tell God plainly, in your own words, what you hope for in love, and write it down to pray with during these nine days.

days.title: Loved Before Anything Else
days.verse: So we know and believe the love God has for us. God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God abides in him.
days.refl: Before we ever love anyone, we are already loved. St. John says it simply: God is love, and whoever abides in love abides in God. Waiting for someone can make us feel overlooked, as if our worth depended on being chosen. It does not. Each of us is known and wanted by God, single or married, now and always. A heart that rests in His love is freer to love others well, without grasping and without fear.
days.more: The Church teaches that God, who created us out of love, also calls us to love: this is the fundamental and innate vocation of every human being (CCC 1604). That call can be lived in marriage, in consecrated life, or as a single person; single people are especially close to Jesus’ heart (CCC 1658). Whatever shape our life takes, love given is never wasted. Today we let God remind us how deeply we are loved.
days.prayer: Loving Father, You loved N. before anyone else did, and Your love does not depend on whether they are single or married. Heal any feeling of being unwanted or forgotten. Let N. rest in Your love, so that they can love others freely and generously. Through the prayers of Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, teach us all to receive Your love, and to share it with everyone we meet.
days.step: Spend five quiet minutes with today’s verse, and hear it as God’s word to you: you are loved, just as you are.

days.title: A Guide on the Road
days.verse: For he will give his angels charge of you / to guard you in all your ways.
days.refl: When young Tobias set out on a long journey, he did not know that his traveling companion was the Archangel Raphael, sent by God. Only at the end did he learn who had walked beside him. Looking for love can feel like walking an unfamiliar road with no map. We do not walk it alone. God guards our ways, often through quiet guidance, good friends and wise advice that we recognize only later. Today we ask Him to guide our steps.
days.more: Raphael did more than keep Tobias safe. Along the way he taught him, protected him at the river, and told him about his kinswoman Sarah. He led him to the house of Sarah’s father, Raguel, and spoke for him when he asked for her hand (Tobit 6–7). That is why St. Raphael has long been invoked by people hoping to meet a good spouse. God’s help often comes through ordinary companions.
days.prayer: Lord God, You sent St. Raphael to walk beside Tobias on a long road. Send Your holy angels to guide N. as well. Lead them to good places and good people, protect them from harm and from anyone who would use them, and give them wise friends who will tell them the truth. Through the prayers of St. Raphael and Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, help us notice Your quiet guidance along the way.
days.step: Ask your guardian angel’s help today, and say yes to one invitation that puts you among good people: a parish event, a class or a gathering of friends.

days.title: Becoming Ready to Love
days.verse: Love is patient and kind; love is not jealous or boastful; it is not arrogant or rude. Love does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice at wrong, but rejoices in the right. Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
days.refl: St. Paul’s description of love is often read at weddings, but it is first a portrait of a heart. Patience, kindness, humility and forgiveness do not suddenly arrive with the right person. They grow in us now, in friendships, families and daily choices. Praying to find love also means asking God to make us someone who can love well. Today we ask Him to heal what is wounded in us and to grow what is good.
days.more: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin lived this kind of love in ordinary work. He was a watchmaker and she ran a lace business in Alençon; in time Louis gave up his own trade to help with hers. They had nine children and buried four of them young. Their letters show tenderness, worry and faith side by side. Holiness grew in them through the patience of daily life, not apart from it.
days.prayer: Lord Jesus, You showed us on the Cross what love is. Make N. patient and kind, humble and forgiving. Heal the wounds and fears that make love hard, and free them from jealousy and selfishness. Through the prayers of Sts. Louis and Zélie, who grew holy in daily life together, prepare N.’s heart now, in family, friendships and work, so that we may all be ready to love and be loved.
days.step: Choose one phrase from today’s verse to practice, such as being patient with someone who tries you, and ask God to help you live it today.

days.title: Wisdom to Recognize
days.verse: And it is my prayer that your love may abound more and more, with knowledge and all discernment, so that you may approve what is excellent, and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ, filled with the fruits of righteousness which come through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
days.refl: St. Paul prays that love will grow together with knowledge and discernment. Wisdom is a gift we can ask for. Choosing someone to share life with is one of the biggest decisions we make, and attraction alone cannot guide it. We need wisdom to look at character more than charm: kindness, faith, honesty and how someone treats others. We need it to notice warning signs, and also to recognize goodness when it is standing right in front of us.
days.more: Sts. Louis and Zélie Martin met in Alençon in 1858. As their family told it, Zélie passed a young man on a bridge and sensed inwardly that this was the one God had prepared for her. They married that July. Not everyone receives such a clear sign, and we should not wait for one. God usually guides us through prayer, good counsel, inner peace and time.
days.prayer: Holy Spirit, giver of wisdom, guide N. in every choice about love. Help them see beyond appearances to the heart, recognize goodness and faith, and notice honestly any warning signs. Give them patience to let trust grow over time, and trusted friends and family whose advice they will listen to. Through the prayers of Sts. Louis and Zélie, keep us from hasty choices and from fear, and lead us in Your peace.
days.step: Ask a trusted friend, family member or priest which qualities they think matter most in a partner for life, and listen with an open mind.

days.title: A Pure & Honest Heart
days.verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, / and put a new and right spirit within me.
days.refl: On their wedding night, Tobias and Sarah rose and prayed together (Tobit 8). Tobias had been afraid, but he trusted God. He told God that he took Sarah as his wife with a sincere heart, not out of lust, and asked that they might grow old together. True love wants the good of the other person, not only what they can give us. It is honest, patient and respectful of body and heart. Today we ask God for a clean heart, and for a love that is pure and free.
days.more: All the baptized are called to chastity, each in the way suited to their state of life (CCC 2348–2349). Chastity is not a fear of love. It integrates our sexuality into the whole person, an apprenticeship in self-mastery that frees us to love (CCC 2337–2339). Where we have fallen short, God’s mercy is greater: Confession gives a fresh start. A clean heart is not a perfect past, but a heart God has made new.
days.prayer: Lord God, Tobias and Sarah began their life together with prayer. Give N. a love that is sincere, chaste and faithful, that seeks the good of the other and never uses anyone. Protect them from relationships that would harm them or lead them away from You, and heal any past mistakes with Your mercy. Through the prayers of Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, create in us clean hearts, honest and free.
days.step: Pray for the person you may one day love, whoever they are, asking God to protect them and keep them close to Him today.

days.title: Trusting God’s Timing
days.verse: When the wine failed, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” And Jesus said to her, “O woman, what have you to do with me? My hour has not yet come.” His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
days.refl: At the wedding in Cana, Mary noticed what others missed: the wine had run out. She told Jesus, and though He said His hour had not yet come, she trusted Him and told the servants to do whatever He said. Waiting for love can make us anxious and impatient, especially when others seem to find it first. Like Mary, we can bring our need to Jesus, then leave the timing to Him, and meanwhile do what He asks of us today.
days.more: One of Mary’s old titles is Mother of Fairest Love, taken from the Book of Sirach in the Latin Bible. It suits her well: she is the mother of Jesus, who is love itself, and she cares about our human joys, as she did at a village wedding. God’s timing is rarely the same as ours, but it is never careless.
days.prayer: Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, as you noticed the need of a young couple at Cana, notice the longing of N. and bring it to your Son. Lord Jesus, we ask You to give N. patience in waiting and peace in uncertainty. Keep them from settling for less out of fear, and from closing their heart out of discouragement. Help us trust that Your hour is the right one.
days.step: Whenever worry about love rises today, pray slowly, “Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, bring this to Jesus,” then turn to the task in front of you.

days.title: Open to God’s Plan
days.verse: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, / neither are your ways my ways, says the LORD. / For as the heavens are higher than the earth, / so are my ways higher than your ways / and my thoughts than your thoughts.
days.refl: God’s ways are higher than ours, Isaiah says, as the heavens are higher than the earth. Our hopes for love may come with a timeline, a type or a picture attached. God may surprise us, in the person, the season, or even the shape of the life He calls us to. Openness is not giving up hope. It is holding our hopes with open hands, trusting that the God who made our hearts knows what will truly fill them.
days.more: Before they met, Louis and Zélie each tried to enter religious life. Louis hoped to join the canons of the Great St. Bernard Hospice in the Alps, but was turned away because he had not learned Latin. Zélie was refused by the Daughters of Charity. Their disappointment became the road to a holy marriage, and to a daughter, St. Thérèse of Lisieux, who became a Doctor of the Church.
days.prayer: Lord, Your thoughts are higher than our thoughts. We place N.’s hopes for love in Your hands. Whether You lead them to marriage or call them to another way of giving their life, give them a generous heart that says yes to You. Through the prayers of Sts. Louis and Zélie, who found Your will through disappointment, free us from fear and fill us with trust.
days.step: Write down one expectation about love that you could hold more loosely, and offer it to God with the words, “Your will be done.”

days.title: Gratitude & Trust in God’s Will
days.verse: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, / and do not rely on your own insight. / In all your ways acknowledge him, / and he will make straight your paths.
days.refl: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, says Proverbs, and He will make your paths straight. We end these nine days not with a demand but with trust. We thank God for every grace He has given, seen and unseen, and we place our hopes for love in His hands. With Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, St. Raphael and Sts. Louis and Zélie, we entrust N.’s heart and future to a Father who is faithful.
days.more: When the journey was over, Raphael told Tobit and Tobias to praise God and give Him thanks (Tobit 12:6). Only then did he tell them who he was. Looking back over these nine days, we may notice small graces: a new friendship, a wiser choice, a calmer heart, a hope renewed. Trusting God’s will does not mean we stop asking. It means we keep praying in peace, knowing that we are loved.
days.prayer: Lord, on this ninth day we thank You for Your faithful love and for every grace You have given N. during these days. Thank you, Mary, Mother of Fairest Love, St. Raphael, and Sts. Louis and Zélie, for carrying our prayers to Jesus. We trust You with N.’s heart and future, with the person they may one day love, and with every step of the road ahead. Your will be done.
days.step: Write down three graces you noticed during these nine days, and thank God for them together.

printClosing: For I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD,
plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope.
